group.title: Hobbies
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: Looking at books and taking in the words for fun.
examples: My mom loves {reading} in bed.
wrong: I do my reading with my ears closed and no book.

words.meaning: Making food hot and ready to eat.
examples: Dad does the {cooking} on Sundays.
wrong: His cooking is a song he plays on the piano.

words.meaning: Making pictures with a brush and colors.
examples: Her hobby is {painting} flowers.
wrong: I do painting with a ball and a goal.

words.meaning: Looking after plants and flowers outside your home.
examples: Grandpa enjoys {gardening} in spring.
wrong: I do gardening in the bath with my rubber duck.

words.meaning: Moving your body to music.
examples: We go {dancing} on Friday night.
wrong: Dancing is when you sit still and do not move.

words.meaning: Making music with your voice.
examples: Her {singing} is very beautiful.
wrong: His singing has no sound at all.

words.meaning: Moving through water with your arms and legs.
examples: I go {swimming} at the pool.
wrong: We do our swimming on the dry road.

words.meaning: Moving very fast on your feet as a sport.
examples: {Running} in the park is good for you.
wrong: Running is a sport you do while you sleep.

words.meaning: Running slowly for exercise.
examples: She goes {jogging} every morning.
wrong: He does his jogging lying on the sofa.

words.meaning: Slow exercise with stretching and calm breathing.
examples: I do {yoga} on a mat at home.
wrong: Yoga is a fast car race.

words.meaning: A game where two teams kick a ball into a goal.
examples: The boys play {soccer} after school.
wrong: In soccer you hit the ball with a bat.

words.meaning: A game where teams hit a ball over a high net with their hands.
examples: We play {volleyball} on the beach.
wrong: In volleyball you kick the ball along the ground.

words.meaning: A game where you hit a ball with a bat and run around four bases.
examples: He hit the ball hard in the {baseball} game.
wrong: Baseball is a game you play in the swimming pool.

words.meaning: A game where you hit a small ball into holes on grass.
examples: My uncle plays {golf} on Saturdays.
wrong: In golf you throw a big ball into a basket.

words.meaning: A game where you hit a small light ball over a net on a table.
examples: We play {table tennis} in the garage.
wrong: Table tennis is a game you play on a big field with a horse.

words.meaning: A game where you hit a light thing with feathers over a high net.
examples: We play {badminton} in the garden.
wrong: In badminton you throw heavy stones into the sea.

words.meaning: A game where you roll a heavy ball to knock down pins.
examples: We went {bowling} for my birthday.
wrong: In bowling you climb a tree with a ball.

words.meaning: A sport from Japan where you fight with your hands and feet.
examples: My sister learns {karate} at a club.
wrong: Karate is a quiet game you play with cards.

words.meaning: A short board with four small wheels that you stand on and ride.
examples: He rides his {skateboard} to the park.
wrong: I eat my soup from a skateboard.

words.meaning: To move on ice or the ground with special shoes that have blades or wheels.
examples: The kids {skate} on the frozen lake.
wrong: I skate on the ice in my bare feet.

words.meaning: A picture in many small pieces that you put back together.
examples: This {puzzle} has a thousand pieces.
wrong: I drink my tea from a puzzle.

words.meaning: A light toy that flies in the wind on a long string.
examples: We fly a {kite} on windy days.
wrong: My kite flies best when there is no wind at all.

words.meaning: A small toy that looks like a person.
examples: The little girl has a {doll} with red hair.
wrong: The doll cooked dinner for the whole family.

words.meaning: A game you play on a screen.
examples: He plays a {video game} on his phone.
wrong: I play my video game on a piece of paper with a pencil.

words.meaning: A thin book that tells a story in pictures.
examples: I read a funny {comic} about a cat.
wrong: A comic has no pictures, only numbers.

words.meaning: Words that tell what happened to people, true or made up.
examples: Mom reads me a {story} at night.
wrong: The story had no people and nothing happened.

words.meaning: A small picture with glue on the back.
examples: She put a star {sticker} on her book.
wrong: My sticker will not stick because it has glue on it.

words.meaning: A round music instrument that you hit with sticks.
examples: He plays the {drum} in a band.
wrong: I play my drum very quietly by blowing into it.

words.meaning: A wooden music instrument with strings that you hold under your chin.
examples: She plays the {violin} in the school band.
wrong: He plays the violin by kicking it.

words.meaning: A long thin music instrument that you blow into.
examples: She plays a sweet song on the {flute}.
wrong: I play the flute by hitting it with a hammer.

words.meaning: Making pictures and other beautiful things.
examples: My favorite class is {art}.
wrong: In art class we only do math.

words.meaning: A metal music instrument that you blow into to make a loud sound.
examples: He plays the {trumpet} very loudly.
wrong: The trumpet makes no sound when you blow into it.

words.meaning: Making or fixing clothes with a needle and thread.
examples: Grandma does her {sewing} by the window.
wrong: She does her sewing with a hammer and nails.

words.meaning: A game where one child looks for the others.
examples: The kids play {hide and seek} in the house.
wrong: In hide and seek everyone stands in the middle of the room.

words.meaning: To walk outside for fun, not to get somewhere.
examples: Let’s {go for a walk} in the park.
wrong: I go for a walk by sitting on the sofa all day.

words.meaning: To look at shows on a television.
examples: We {watch TV} after dinner.
wrong: I watch TV with my eyes closed.

words.meaning: Sitting on a horse and moving on it for fun or sport.
examples: She goes {horse riding} on the farm.
wrong: I go horse riding on my bicycle.

words.meaning: To sleep outside in a tent.
examples: We {camp} by the lake every summer.
wrong: We camp in a big hotel room.

words.meaning: To hear songs for fun.
examples: I {listen to music} on the bus.
wrong: I listen to music on my mute phone with no sound.

words.meaning: A trip on a bicycle.
examples: We went for a {bike ride} by the river.
wrong: We went on a bike ride in a car.
